As a an AITM operator
I want to Full-Auto to be the default while opting into manual plan, PR-code, or final task review gates
So that unattended delivery runs without babysitting while explicit human review requests remain enforceable and auditable

## Scope

Make Full-Auto the default operating mode for AITM sessions.

Users must be able to opt into explicit review gates using natural requests:

- "manual plan review" pauses for human approval of the plan before implementation.
- "manual code review" pauses for human approval after implementation/code review before delivery.
- "manual task review" pauses at the final Review-to-Done boundary before close.

The design must define precedence, scope, persistence, help text, audit provenance, and safe behavior when multiple manual-review requests are combined. Existing governed evidence, delivery, worktree, and close protections must remain intact.

## User Story

As an AITM operator
I want Full-Auto to be the default while retaining explicit manual review controls
So that unattended delivery runs without babysitting and requested human judgments remain enforceable and auditable

## Scope

Make Full-Auto the default operating mode for new AITM sessions. Preserve three independent, session-scoped manual-review controls that users can request in natural language:

- "manual plan review" pauses for human plan approval before implementation.
- "manual code review" allows the PR to reach green required CI, requests an eligible configured or authenticated user as reviewer, skips spawned-agent PR implementation review as approval authority, and requires that human's approval of the exact PR head before merge authority is emitted.
- "manual task review" pauses at the final Review-to-Done boundary before close.

Multiple manual-review requests combine additively. The most recent explicit request for a gate wins for that gate, session overrides outrank project configuration, and reset returns to the new Full-Auto defaults. Reviewer assignment is an affordance rather than proof: an assignment never counts as approval, the PR author cannot approve their own work, and missing or ineligible reviewer authority fails closed with actionable remediation. Existing evidence, exact-SHA delivery, CI, worktree, ownership, provider-action, and close protections remain mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New sessions default the plan, PR-code, and final-task review controls to Full-Auto without emitting the legacy first-bind mode prompt.
- [ ] A user request for "manual plan review" enables only the Plan-to-Develop human approval gate unless other manual gates were also explicitly requested.
- [ ] A user request for "manual code review" waits until required CI is green, requests an eligible configured or authenticated user on the PR when needed, and requires a human approval tied to the exact accepted PR head before merge authority; reviewer assignment alone and spawned-agent review are insufficient.
- [ ] A user request for "manual task review" enables only the final Review-to-Done human approval gate unless other manual gates were also explicitly requested.
- [ ] Manual review controls are independent, additive, session-scoped, auditable, and governed by session-over-project-over-default precedence; reset restores Full-Auto defaults.
- [ ] CLI help, agent workflow instructions, and user documentation name the three natural-language requests and explain reviewer eligibility, approval freshness, combinations, and reset behavior.
- [ ] Existing exact-SHA evidence, required-CI, delivery receipt, ownership, worktree, provider-action, and close protections remain enforced, with focused regression coverage for legacy two-gate session files and explicit project configuration.
